The play combines a heartfelt story about dealing with the loss of loved ones with lush set design and perfectly timed lighting cues to create a spectacle that is a feast for the ears, eyes and heart.
Shattered Globe Theatre’s latest offering unveils a lovely, soulful story about hope and healing and so much more.

Director Amber Montgomery, a rising star, skillfully balances comedy and drama in Jump, which provides an inspiring testament to the power of love and the need for understanding the mental health of loved ones.
Shattered Globe's Midwest premiere production, directed with kinetic flair by AmBer Montgomery, explores these themes in authentic, moving and often-surprising ways.
This production certainly meets its program's goal of 'bridging heartbreak and hope.'
The acting and sets are really good, the climax gives a surprising and satisfying resolution.
The best part of this show is its focus on the unpredictability of suicide and how death affects those who must live with its consequences.

cn.t: Simpson's magical realist drama about suicide and grief earns praise for its dazzling lead performance and kinetic direction, though critics are divided on whether its quirky, mystical approach fully succeeds in exploring its heavy themes.
